sDescription: Ed Sheeran was at No.1 on the UK chart with his eighth studio album Play. It was the first of Sheeran's planned pentalogy of albums titled after media control symbols, with Pause, Fast Forward, Rewind, and Stop to follow. The album gave Sheeran his eighth top-10-charting album on the US Billboard 200, where it peaked at No.5.

American session musician, orchestra leader, and double bassist Bob Moore died age 88. He was a member of the Nashville A-Team during the 1950s and 1960s and performed on over 17,000 documented recording sessions, backing acts such as Elvis Presley, Patsy Cline, Bob Dylan and Roy Orbison.

Paul McCartney was at No.1 on the US chart with his 17th solo studio album Egypt Station. The name 'Egypt Station' is shared by one of McCartney's paintings from 1988, from which the cover art is derived. It became his first No.1 album in the US since 1982's Tug of War and his first to debut atop the Billboard 200.

English musician and singer Chas Hodges died from pneumonia on aged 74. Hodges had worked with British producer Joe Meek as a session musician, backing Jerry Lee Lewis and Gene Vincent. He later joined Heads Hands and Feet, (with guitarist Albert Lee). With Chas & Dave he scored the 1982 UK No.2 single 'Ain't No Pleasing You'. He also played piano for short-lived supergroup the Rockers, which featured Roy Wood, Phil Lynott and John Coghlan.

A US District Judge ruled that the original copyright to 'Happy Birthday' was invalid and the song would now be entirely in the public domain. The copyright was obtained by the Clayton F. Summy Co. from the song's writers, sisters Mildred and Patty Hill and bought for $15 million in 1988 by Warner / Chappell Music Inc.

Research conducted by car maker SEAT found that Queen’s 'Bohemian Rhapsody' was the song most likely to be found on British iPods, with more than 40% of owners having the hit on their players. The Beatles had four songs in the list, a feat also matched by Coldplay. Other favourites included U2, The Killers and Rihanna.

Britney Spears was charged with hit-and-run and driving without a valid licence after she was accused of hitting a parked car and driving away from a Los Angeles car park on 6 August. The owner of the car filed an accident report on 9 August at the North Hollywood Community Police Station. The city attorney's office did not know whether Ms Spears' car had been damaged, nor did he know the extent of damage to the other car.

The Game was given a conditional discharge at Manhattan's Criminal Court after being charged with impersonating a police officer. Police said the star told a cab driver he was an undercover officer, ordering him to run several red lights. The rapper (real name Jayceon Taylor), claimed the cab driver noticed they were being followed and asked who was in the car, He said he told the driver they were the hip-hop police, and the driver decided on his own to run the red lights.

Jimmy Page was made an honorary citizen of Brazilian city Rio de Janeiro for his work helping its street children. The Led Zeppelin guitarist had opened Casa Jimmy (Jimmy's House) in 1998 which had so far supported more than 300 children.

Cat Stevens, who now went by the name of Yusuf Islam, was escorted from a diverted transatlantic flight and refused entry into America by FBI agents. His name showed up on a US watch list after United Airlines Flight 919 had taken off from London. The flight landed in Maine where Islam, who was traveling with his 21-year-old daughter, was detained and questioned.

‘A Tribute to Heroes’ was aired commercial-free on most of the major US TV networks. The live program was organised to raise money following the terrorist attacks on the Pentagon and New York’s World Trade Center. Neil Young, Tom Petty, Paul Simon, Billy Joel, U2, Limp Bizkit, Bruce Springsteen and Pearl Jam all performed. Manning the telephones to take pledges were celebrities including Jack Nicholson, Jim Carrey, Whoopi Goldberg, Goldie Hawn, Robin Williams, Meg Ryan, Cuba Gooding Jr., Kurt Russell, Adam Sandler and many more.

Diana Ross was arrested on Concorde after an incident at Heathrow Airport. The singer claimed that a female security guard had touched her breasts when being frisked; Ross retaliated by rubbing her hands down the security guard.

Def Leppard were forced to cancel two US shows after their sound-equipment truck was found abandoned, after one of the bands driver's had attempted to rob a store. The driver was later charged of possessing drugs and criminal damage.

Bryan Adams made chart history when '(Everything I Do), I Do It For You', had its twelfth consecutive week as the UK No.1 single. The track went on to spend sixteen consecutive weeks at No.1, the longest uninterrupted run ever on that chart as of 2025.

Nirvana played their biggest gig to date when they appeared at the Motor Sports International Garage in Seattle. Drummer Dave Grohl who would audition for the band in a few days time was in the audience of 15,000 people.

The Garth Brooks album No Fences entered the US album chart. It went on to become the biggest-selling country album of all time. No Fences remains Brooks' best-selling studio album to date, with 18 million copies shipped in the US. Some of Brooks' most famous songs appear on the album, including 'The Thunder Rolls' (CMA's 1991 Video of the Year) and 'Friends in Low Places' (Academy of Country Music's 1990 Single of the Year).

The first Farm Aid benefit concert was held before a crowd of 80,000 people at the Memorial Stadium in Champaign, Illinois. Organized by Willie Nelson, John Mellencamp and Neil Young, the event had been spurred on by Bob Dylan's comments at Live Aid earlier in that year that he hoped some of the money would help American farmers. The star studded line-up of country stars included: Alabama, Hoyt Axton, Glen Campbell, Johnny Cash, Charlie Daniels Band, John Denver, Bob Dylan, John Fogerty, Vince Gill, Merle Haggard, Emmylou Harris, Waylon Jennings, George Jones, Kris Kristofferson, Loretta Lynn, Roger Miller, Nitty Gritty Dirt Band, Willie Nelson, Charley Pride, Bonnie Raitt, Kenny Rogers.

American composer Harry Warren died aged 88. He wrote over 800 songs including 'I Only Have Eyes For You', (a hit for The Flamingos and Art Garfunkel), ‘You Must Have Been a Beautiful Baby’, ‘Jeepers Creepers’, ‘That's Amore’ and ‘Chattanooga Choo Choo’. Warren's songs have been featured in over 300 films.

Def Leppard had their first major live review when UK music weekly Melody Maker reviewed a gig the band had played at the Lafayette Club in Wolverhampton. The show featured the early lineup of Joe Elliott, Rick Savage, Pete Willis, Steve Clark, and 15-year-old drummer Rick Allen.

Gary Numan had his second and final UK No.1 single with 'Cars'. Also on this day, Gary Numan went to No.1 on the UK album chart with his debut solo studio album, The Pleasure Principle. Although Numan had a string of hits in the UK, 'Cars' was his only song to reach the American pop charts.

The Rolling Stones scored their eighth UK No.1 album when Goats Head Soup started a two-week run at the top of the charts. Like its predecessor Exile on Main St., the band composed and recorded much of it outside of the United Kingdom due to their status as tax exiles — specifically, in Jamaica and the United States. The album contains 10 tracks, including the lead single 'Angie', which went to No.1 as a single in the US and the top five in the UK.

David Bowie kicked of the North American leg of his Ziggy Stardust world tour at the Music Hall in Cleveland, Ohio. The 191 date tour lasted a year and a half and included three legs in the UK, two in the US and one in Japan.

The Band released their self-titled album, which peaked at No.9 on the US chart, and included the tracks; 'Rag Mama Rag', 'Up on Cripple Creek' and 'The Night They Drove Old Dixie Down'. In 2009, the album was preserved into the National Recording Registry because the album was ‘culturally, historically, or aesthetically important, and reflects life in the United States.’

A new weekly TV show 'The Music Scene' aired on ABC in the US for the first time. Stevie Wonder, Crosby Stills Nash & Young, Tom Jones, Cass Elliot, James Brown, Janis Joplin and Sly and the Family Stone were all booked to appear on the show.

The Doors appeared on the Murray the K show on WPIX-TV in New York City performing 'People Are Strange' and 'Light My Fire.' Murray the K, was a New York City rock and roll impresario and disc jockey of the 1950s, 1960s and 1970s. During the early days of Beatlemania, he frequently referred to himself as the fifth Beatle.
San Francisco band The Great Society, featuring Grace Slick and her then-husband Jerry Slick on drums, made their live debut at The Coffee Gallery, North Beach, California.

English pop rock group Herman's Hermits were at No.1 on the UK singles chart with the Carole King & Gerry Goffin song 'I'm Into Something Good', the group's only UK No.1. The song was originally recorded by Cookies member Earl-Jean on Colpix Records in 1964. Her version entered the US Top 100 charts, peaking at No.42.

The Springfields (Dusty Springfield her brother Tom and their friend, Tim Field) had 'Silver Threads and Golden Needles', enter the US Top 20 and became the first British vocal group to chart that high in America.

After receiving special permission from the US Army, Elvis Presley gave one last press conference at the Military Ocean Terminal in Brooklyn. He then joined the rest of the 3rd Armored Division on the USS General Randall for a voyage to Bremerhaven, Germany.

South Korean singer Nayeon who rose to prominence as a member of the South Korean girl group Twice, created by JYP Entertainment through the reality television show Sixteen (2015). Twice scored the 2024 US No.1 album With You-th.
DeMario DeWayne White Jr. known professionally as Moneybagg Yo, American rapper. His fourth album, A Gangsta's Pain, released in April 2021 became his first chart-topping album on the US chart.

Will Farquarson, bass and guitar with English indie pop band Bastille who had a No.1 UK album with Bad Blood (2013), which included the hit single 'Pompeii' which peaked at No.2 on the UK Singles Chart.

English singer and actress Billie Piper. She initially gained recognition as a singer after releasing her debut single 'Because We Want To' at the age of 15, which made her the youngest female singer to enter the UK Singles Chart at No.1. In 2003, Piper announced that she had ended her music career to focus on acting.

American rapper and actor Mystikal, (Michael Tyler). He had the 2001 US No.1 & UK No.7 single 'Stutter'. In 2004, he was sentenced to six years in prison after pleading guilty to forcing his hairstylist to perform sex acts.
Andy Cairns, guitar, vocals with the alternative metal band from Northern Ireland Therapy? who had the 1993 UK No.9 single 'Screamager'.

American rock guitarist, singer, songwriter, and producer Joan Jett. She was a founding member of The Runaways and with Joan Jett & the Blackhearts, scored the 1982 US No.1 & UK No.4 single I Love Rock ‘n’ Roll. She is also known as the Godmother of Punk.

Italian tenor Andrea Bocelli. His sight was impaired from birth due to congenital glaucoma and age 12, Bocelli lost his vision completely after being hit in the eye with a football. He rose to fame in 1994 after winning the newcomers section of the 44th Sanremo Music Festival, performing 'Il mare calmo della sera'. A version of Time to Say Goodbye sung partly in English, released in 1996, paired Bocelli with British soprano Sarah Brightman, topped charts all across Europe, including Germany, where it became one of the biggest-selling singles in history.

Australian singer, songwriter Nick Cave, who fronted the Birthday Party, one of the most extreme and confrontational post-punk bands of the early 1980s. He had the 1995 UK No.11 single with Kylie Minogue, 'Where The Wild Roses Grow'. In 2006, he formed the garage rock band Grinderman.
Peter Jones from the English post-punk band Public Image Ltd, formed by lead vocalist John Lydon. They scored the 1983 UK No.5 single 'This Is Not A Love Song'.

American bassist Douglas Wimbish known for being a member of rock band Living Colour and funk/dub/hip hop collective Tackhead, and as a session musician with artists such as Sugarhill Gang, Grandmaster Flash and the Furious Five, The Rolling Stones, Mick Jagger, Depeche Mode, James Brown and Annie Lennox.

Debby Boone, US singer. Daughter of 50s singer Pat Boone. Ten weeks at No.1 on the US singles chart with 'You Light Up My Life', in 1977. The longest stay at the top of the charts since Guy Mitchell's 'Singing The Blues. A No.48 in the UK.

American musician Rhett Forrester best known as the lead singer for New York-based band Riot from 1981 until 1984. Forrester was shot and killed at a Northwest Atlanta intersection after he refused to give up his vehicle in an attempted carjacking, he was 37 years old.

English singer and television presenter Richard Fairbrass, who with Right Said Fred, scored the 1991 US No.1 & UK No.2 single ‘I’m Too Sexy’, and the 1993 UK No.1 album Up. Before forming his own band, Fairbrass was a bassist who had played with several prominent artists, including Boy George. In 1984, he appeared in Jazzin' for Blue Jean, a video by David Bowie, as the bass player.
Mark Panker, guitarist with the San Francisco-based indie rock band American Music Club. Formed in 1982, the band released seven albums before splitting up in 1995.

English singer and songwriter David Coverdale, who, with Whitesnake, scored the 1987 US No.1 & UK No.9 single 'Here I Go Again'. Coverdale was the lead singer of Deep Purple from late 1973 to March 1976. From 1990 to 1993, Coverdale collaborated with Led Zeppelin guitarist Jimmy Page on the album Coverdale–Page.
Toni Basil, US singer actress and dancer, (1982 US No.1 & UK No.2 single 'Mickey'). Basil worked as David Bowie's choreographer on his Diamond Dogs tour in 1974 and on his Glass Spider tour of 1987.

English musician Mike Patto who was primarily notable as lead singer for Spooky Tooth and Boxer. He first became vocalist and frontman for The Bo Street Runners, who won a TV band competition Ready Steady Win during 1964. Patto died of throat cancer on 4 March 1979 aged 36.

American singer Raymond Edwards from The Silhouettes. The doo wop/R&B groups single 'Get A Job' was a No.1 hit on the Billboard R&B singles chart and pop singles chart in 1958. The doo-wop revival group Sha Na Na derived their name from the song's lyrics. 'Get A Job' is included in the soundtracks of the film American Graffiti, Trading Places and Stand By Me. Edwards died on March 4th 1997.
